articles.title: BNP, Awami League supporters clash in Bangladesh amid political unrest
articles.summary: Dhaka: Supporters of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the banned Awami League clashed in several parts of the country amid escalating political violence, prompting the deployment of hundreds of additional paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel. The clashes came even as Jamaat-e-Islami, the main parliamentary opposition party, on Saturday launched a 40-day nationwide protest, coinciding with the planned return of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India next month, despite her death sentence. Dozens of homes and shops belonging to Awami League leaders and activists were vandalised and set ablaze in Narail's Kalia upazila on Friday, the Dhaka Tribune reported. Bangladesh minister vows action against those behind arson, blames Awami League-linked groups: reports The attacks followed the killing of two BNP-affiliated leaders in the area on Wednesday. The violence swept through Bendar Char village from Friday afternoon into the night, targeting properties associated with the banned Awami League members, The Dhaka Tribune reported. The fire service reported damage to around 20 to 30 homesteads. Clashes also broke out between BNP and Awami League supporters in Bera upazila of Pabna district on Saturday, The Daily Star reported. The violence began around 11 am and continued into the afternoon, prompting police to fire rubber bullets and teargas shells to bring the situation under control, it said. According to police and local sources, tensions had been simmering for three days across several neighbourhoods of Bera municipality, including Payna, Brishalikha, Sawdagorpara and Hatigara, over attempts to establish supremacy. The tensions were marked by protest rallies, chases and counter-chases, the report said. An Awami League leader, speaking from a secret location in Dhaka, alleged that party supporters had faced sustained persecution. "We have been on the run for over two years when hundreds of our supporters were lynched or wounded, and thousands more are languishing in jails," he said. "We have been pushed to the brink, which left us with no other option but to stand back and resist," he said, adding that "many of our family members are virtually starving as we are kicked out of businesses or jobs". Three BNP-affiliated leaders, including the two killed in Narail's Kalia, were killed in separate incidents earlier this week. A bus helper was also burnt alive after unidentified assailants set fire to parked buses, The Dhaka Tribune reported. In the past week, at least three police stations were torched, including two in Hasina's home district of Gopalganj. The ancestral home of former interim government chief Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram and dozens of branches of his Grameen Bank across the country were also targeted, according to media reports. State-run BSS news agency reported on Saturday that 90 additional BGB platoons had been deployed across the country. Meanwhile, Jamaat secretary general Mia Mohammad Porwar alleged at a press conference that Awami League activists had resorted to sabotage, arson and violence following Hasina's plan to return to Bangladesh. "These incidents are not confined to Gopalganj; violence has occurred in 22 districts (out of 64)," he said. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday also accused Hasina's Awami League of conspiring to destabilise Bangladesh. On Wednesday, Rahman asked BNP lawmakers to return immediately to their constituencies and establish a visible and strong presence on the streets alongside grassroots workers to counter the Awami League, rather than relying solely on government machinery or the administration. State Minister for Local Government Mir Shahe Alam on Saturday said that, if required, the Awami League would be "permanently banned" under a consensus with Jamaat, as the "time has come to think anew" about the possibility. Earlier on Friday, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir blamed the Awami League for the escalation in violence, saying Bangladesh would take firm legal action against those behind recent arson and petrol bomb attacks. After Sheikh Hasina, 7 more Awami League leaders get death sentence in Bangladesh "We will go after these terrorists, and the long arm of justice will reach them," he said, responding to questions from reporters on the sidelines of a media briefing, according to the state-run BSS news agency. Kobir alleged that the Awami League leadership was encouraging the attacks from abroad and that others based overseas were also involved in efforts to instigate violence. In separate remarks at the foreign ministry, Kobir described the Awami League, whose political activities remain banned, as a "terrorist organisation" and warned of strong action against those involved in petrol bomb attacks, arson and other violence, The Daily Star reported. On the return of fugitives from abroad, Kobir said attempts to bring them back from New Delhi through acts of violence would not succeed, as their return would be pursued under the extradition treaty. Hasina's proposed return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi. The latest wave of unrest followed the Bangladesh government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December. Her passport and national identity card had been revoked by the interim government after she fled Bangladesh in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. The Awami League subsequently announced a week-long programme of protests demanding her return, culminating in a nationwide shutdown on November 19. Hasina has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024. Her extradition has remained a point of friction between the two countries, with both the interim administration led by Muhammad Yunus and the subsequent BNP government headed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman pressing New Delhi to hand her over under a bilateral extradition treaty. Dhaka has insisted that Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters, must be brought back from India under the bilateral extradition treaty rather than allowed to return as an ordinary traveller. Hasina has said she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and surrender before a court. She has denied the charges against her.

The charges relate to alleged sexual offences involving a minor between September 4 and 26, 2026. The case was filed on November 6 before the San Diego Superior Court. According to the court’s online records, Bhaskar faces two counts of oral copulation of a person under 18 and two counts of sexual penetration with a foreign object involving a victim under 18. The court records also show that a warrant was issued on November 6, the day the complaint was filed. The San Diego Superior Court confirmed to TNM that the complaint lists four charges and that the alleged offences took place “on or about and between September 4, 2026 and September 26, 2026.” The court said no date had been scheduled for Bhaskar’s arraignment and that he had not made any in-court appearances as of November 21. It could not confirm whether he was in custody. However, a source told TNM that Bhaskar is currently in custody at a jail in Boston, Massachusetts. The court's Public Affairs Office told TNM that this was possible and said he could also be awaiting an extradition hearing for his transfer to California. Carnatic vocalist TM Krishna, who described Bhaskar as a colleague with whom he had shared numerous stages and a friend of over two decades, issued a public statement on the allegations. Saying that the past week had been difficult, Krishna said he felt “a lot of anger and profound sadness” over the accusations. He reiterated his commitment to “justice for survivors” and said he could not comment further as investigations were underway in the US. He has trained under violinists MS Gopalakrishnan and RN Thyagarajan and is an A-grade violinist of All India Radio and Doordarshan.

articles.title: COP31 talks drag on as nations remain divided over fossil fuel phase-out
articles.summary: New Delhi: Negotiations at the UN climate summit in Turkey extended into “extra time” on Saturday, as consensus on the outcome document remained elusive amid deep divisions among nations over how the text should address fossil fuel emissions in an increasingly warming world, while also taking into account the Global South’s demand for economic growth. Negotiators worked through the night to try to break the deadlock over energy, finance and science, as the summit went past its scheduled closing time on Friday without an agreement. Saudi Arabia, Russia and India are among the countries understood to have opposed any decisive reference to the “phase-out of fossil fuels” in the text. From the outset of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, references to fossil fuels remained central to the deadlock, pushing the summit into overtime. COP31 President Murat Kurum urged nations on Saturday to “act responsibly” and reach a compromise, as negotiators remained divided over a deal acceptable to all. “I call on everyone to act responsibly... Getting bogged down in individual words and expressions and undermining this process serves no one's interests,” said Kurum, who is also Turkey’s Environment Minister. COP33: India withdraws bid to host UN climate summit in 2028 The European Union’s climate envoy said no compromise had been reached on key sticking points blocking an agreement at the UN climate talks. “Clearly there's no compromise yet,” EU Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said in Antalya. “It's better to have no deal than to have a bad deal.” While the initial draft presented by the COP presidency, led by Turkey and Australia, called for an immediate and accelerated phase-out of fossil fuels, the second draft published on Thursday removed the term altogether. The omission triggered a sharp diplomatic dispute. Environmentalists claimed that efforts to phase out fossil fuels were being sidelined by the COP31 presidencies, while finance commitments were missing and clean electrification risked being diluted through carbon capture and fossil fuel loopholes. With the Indian delegation, led by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav, scheduled to return on Sunday, the team has a few more hours to negotiate. Presenting India’s statement earlier this week, Yadav said the Global South could not be made to bear the burden of emission cuts in the name of “higher ambition”, arguing that global warming was the consequence of “unabashed greenhouse gas emission for two centuries” by industrialised nations. The last time, a COP ended in time was in Italy in 2003.

He lost the 2018 Assembly election to BJP’s Raghupathi Bhat and unsuccessfully contested the 2019 Lok Sabha polls on a Janata Dal (Secular) ticket. articles.title: Ladakh records over 70% turnout in first local polls since UT formation
articles.summary: Srinagar: More than 70 per cent of voters participated in Ladakh ’s panchayat elections on Saturday, marking the return of grassroots electoral institutions in the cold desert region after an eight-year gap and its first such exercise since it became a Union Territory in 2019. The panchayat elections recorded 73.60 per cent turnout in panch constituencies and 70.03 per cent in sarpanch constituencies, while municipal elections in Leh and Kargil registered an overall turnout of 52.40 per cent, according to figures shared by Lieutenant Governor V.K. Saxena. Saxena described the polling as a “historic day”, saying participation in the panchayat elections had improved over the 67.8 per cent turnout recorded in the 2018 elections. The elections are significant for Ladakh, which has been without elected panchayats and municipal councils for several years. The previous local body elections were held in 2018, when the region was part of the erstwhile Jammu and Kashmir state. Ladakh votes after eight years as debate over political representation remains unresolved The electoral exercise comes amid an ongoing political debate over Ladakh’s future, with the Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) demanding statehood, constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule and protection of land, employment and cultural identity. Unlike Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh does not have a legislative assembly following its separation from the erstwhile state in August 2019. Its administration is headed by a Lieutenant Governor, while the two Autonomous Hill Development Councils, panchayats and municipal bodies provide elected representation at different levels. The latest elections will restore elected institutions at the village and municipal levels, but the larger demand for a stronger political and constitutional framework remains unresolved. The panchayat elections covered 192 halqas across Ladakh’s eight districts, with 192 sarpanch and 1,428 panch positions. Of these, 55 sarpanches and 1,186 panches were elected unopposed, leaving 137 sarpanch and 242 panch seats for polling. The municipal elections covered 38 wards in Leh and Kargil. Polling was held in all 21 wards of Leh, while candidates in four of Kargil’s 17 wards were elected unopposed, leaving 13 wards to go to the polls. The administration deployed special arrangements to conduct polling in the region’s geographically difficult terrain. In Zanskar, helicopter services were used to airlift polling teams to three remote polling stations that were inaccessible by road. The high turnout also comes ahead of the December 4 elections to the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils, covering 100 constituencies. For the first time, 36 of these seats have been reserved for women.

articles.title: Karnataka HC sets aside order replacing C T Puttaswamy as Forest Dept Technical Cell Director
articles.summary: Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has set aside the order of replacing C T Putttaswamy as Director (Technical Cell) Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment. On July 24, 2026, an order was passed replacing Puttaswamy by appointing B R Ramesh, an IFS officer. It was stated in the petition that Putttaswamy, who was earlier working as Professor, Department of Chemical Engineering at BMS Engineering College, was appointed on contract basis in the post of Director (Technical Cell) Department of Forest, Ecology and Environment. The tenure was specified as for one year commencing from January 27, 2025, or until further orders. The tenure was extended by one year on January 27, 2026. While his extended tenure was till January 2027, IFS officer BR Ramesh was appointed on July 24, 2026. On the other hand, the state government argued that Putttaswamy’s appointment on contract basis was specified as “until further orders" and that employees serving under deputation possess no indefeasible legal right to continue in such a borrowed post. After perusing the materials, Justice Sunil Dutt Yadav noted that the order extending tenure specifically recited that the petitioner's appointment was subject to the original order of appointment on contract, which was extended for a period of one year from January 27, 2026, on contractual basis. Karnataka HC orders state govt to identify forests, forest-like areas in state The court further noted that the petitioner being employed in a private engineering college, which is not a Department of Government, but a University, is by virtue of the Rules allowed a lateral entry to the post of a senior official Director, Technical Cell. “While a deputationist may not normally have an indefeasible right to continue, though law does extend protection against arbitrariness, the posting of the petitioner as described above would confer further qualitative protection by virtue of it being a deputation by appointment and not a deputation by transfer. The replacement of the petitioner by the IFS officer is with immediate effect and factually, the petitioner has been displaced contemporaneous to the order of replacement However, the said order does not assign any reason for displacing the petitioner which would fall within the description of arbitrary or capricious,” Justice Yadav said. The court further said,” The petitioner would be entitled to continue in service till January 27, 2027. In light of his being relieved of duties, he is entitled for reinstatement and entitled to pay from the date of the impugned order till date. The direction for reinstatement to be adhered to forthwith and in any event not later than one week from today.” The court meanwhile declined the prayer made by petitioner for extending his service till January 26, 2028.

Those attending the event included Azerbaijan’s Minister of Culture Adil Karimli, Nepal’s Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation Khadga Raj Poudel (Ganesh), and Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture Matlubakhon Amonzoda Sattoriyon. Representatives from Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Cambodia, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and other countries also participated.

articles.title: Anjali Ambiger murder case: Hubballi court convicts Girish Savant; sentence to be pronounced on Nov 25
articles.summary: Hubballi: In a major development in the sensational 2024 murder case of Anjali Ambiger, which made national headlines, a court in Hubballi has convicted the accused, Girish Savant. The court will pronounce the quantum of punishment on November 25. Hearing the case on Saturday, the First Additional District and Sessions Court convicted Girish under sections relating to house trespass with intent to commit an offence, murder and causing the disappearance of evidence. The accused presented before the court via video conference from Hubballi jail. First Additional District and Sessions Judge Pallavi B R also gave the accused an opportunity to present his views on the quantum of punishment. Accordingly, the court scheduled November 25 for a hearing on the sentence and directed him to appear. On May 15, 2024, 20-year-old Anjali Ambiger was murdered at her residence in Veerapur Oni, Hubballi. The accused, Girish Savant, alias Vishwa, fled the scene after committing the crime. He was subsequently arrested by the police on May 17, 2024. Anjali Ambiger murder accused caught Anjali Ambiger murder case: Bendigeri Police Inspector, woman head constable suspended The murder took place barely a month after Neha Hiremath was killed by a friend on her college campus in Hubballi. As two young women were murdered within a month in the city, both cases triggered widespread public outrage and attracted national attention. Subsequently, the investigation into Anjali's murder was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). Following its investigation, the CID filed a 494-page charge sheet against Girish Savant, listing 85 witnesses. The government appointed advocate R K Kale as the Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) to represent the prosecution. During the trial, the prosecution examined 46 witnesses and produced 18 material objects before the court. Several organisations and political leaders have welcomed the court's verdict and expressed satisfaction over the conviction. Attention has now turned to November 25, when the court is expected to announce the sentence. Meanwhile, the trial in the Neha Hiremath murder case is still pending, with a final hearing expected to take place soon.
